Targeted pass of an 820-page BREF. Locators are PRINTED page numbers (PDF page = printed + 42). Read: TOC; Sect. 2.1.2 and 2.2.1 (energy), 2.3.2 (energy-efficiency techniques: heat recovery Table 2.39, CHP, insulation, VSD, economiser, blowdown Table 2.40, multistage evaporation, MVR/TVR Table 2.41); sector energy sections and energy techniques of Ch. 3 (animal feed / green fodder), 4 (brewing, Tables 4.1 and 4.3), 5 (dairies, Tables 5.5-5.7, regeneration, multistage drying), 6 (ethanol, Table 6.2 DDGS), 7 (fish), 8 (fruit and vegetables, peeling and blanching Tables 8.2-8.9, 8.15-8.16, freezing), 11 (oil refining vacuum Tables 11.1-11.3, DT Table 11.10), 12, 13 (incl. emerging Table 13.1), 14, 15 (beet pulp drying), 16 (pasta, bakery, tartaric acid); Ch. 17 BAT conclusions indicative specific energy consumption levels (Tables 17.2, 17.5, 17.8, 17.12, 17.14, 17.16, 17.19, 17.23, 17.25, 17.28); Annex 19.2.5-19.2.6 (evaporation, freezing). A full-document grep for kWh/MWh/GJ/MJ/kJ/kcal/steam was used to catch numbers outside these sections. Main file: 19 BAT-conclusion whole-site SEC benchmarks (heat plus electricity, target blank, MWh/t or MWh/hl as printed; activity rate varies: products, raw materials, oil produced, beets) plus text whole-site SECs (distillery, fish filleting/canning, Spanish tomato, pasta, tartaric acid, olive mill, brewery); evaporators (single/double/triple effect steam t/t water evaporated, TVR 3-7 stages and MVR kWh/kg water evaporated, Japanese dairy MVR vs TVR costs); dryers (two-stage dairy spray+FBD, beet-pulp HTD, DDGS, green-fodder exhaust heat recovery costs); pasteurisers (milk with/without regeneration, UHT with/without heat recovery, juice 95/80 degC); blanchers and peelers (steam t/t and kWhe/t frozen product); freezing tunnels; bakery ovens; boilers and CHP efficiencies; oilseed DT; deodoriser vacuum systems. Measures file: techniques with savings and/or costs. Not loaded: graph-only data (sector SEC figures 3.11, 4.12, 5.12-5.15, 8.6, 9.1, 10.2, 11.6-11.7, 13.1, 14.8, 15.3 have no printed numbers), water, waste water, dust/NOX/TVOC and odour (non-GHG), noise. The TWG treated plant-level SEC data as confidential, so only BAT ranges and text values are printed. Steam given as mass (t/t, kg/t) is kept in the source unit in specific-energy-consumption rows with target steam. Most costs carry no price year (2019 used and flagged); Japanese dairy, Danish/UK examples are reprints of COM 2006 / Nordic Council 2001 data.

(1) Single-stage evaporator steam 1.2-1.4 t/t (p.93) vs 1.1-1.2 t/t (Annex p.745). (2) Steam peeling pressure 7-15 bar (Table 8.2) vs 4-15 bar (Table 8.16) for the same 0.9 t/t. (3) Blancher electricity in text differs from tables (belt/water 2-8 vs 2-9; belt/air 7-28 vs 7-30; drum 1-2.6 incl. cooling vs 0.5-1.3). (4) Table 11.2 dry-condensing steam 5.5-15.5 kWh/t printed beside 20-150 kg/t, inconsistent with ~0.78 kWh/kg elsewhere. (5) Table 11.10 DT values per "t" with no stated product (seeds or meal). (6) Biogas CHP capacity printed as "600 kWh electrical and 600 kWh thermal". (7) Finnish MVR "100-125 kg of water using 1 kW". (8) Table 5.6 units "kW/h" and "kw/year". (9) BAT SEC activity rates differ by sector (products, raw materials, oil, beets, hl). (10) Heating-value basis never stated except boiler efficiency (lowest calorific value).
